summary: Today’s pulse tracks Walter Koenig, actor best known as Chekov on Star Trek, dies aged 90, Southern California prepares for flooding amid forecast of ‘record-breaking tides’, and Judge says DOJ illegally fired the daughter of former FBI director Comey. Across Guardian, NPR, and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are flooding, actor, and coastal. In the background, Republican and Democratic ex-governors issue rare joint endorsement for South Carolina Senate candidate – US politics live and Lula wins fourth term in dramatic Brazil election comeback keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Walter Koenig, actor best known as Chekov on Star Trek, dies aged 90
headlines.description: The actor appeared in the cult 1960s show as well as many of the films but also worked as a writer Walter Koenig, the actor known for playing Pavel Chekov throughout the Star Trek franchise, has died, his representative confirmed to the Hollywood Reporter . He was 90. Koenig died at his home in North Hollywood surrounded by his daughter and niece, according to a Facebook post by Zachery McGinnis, the founder of Galactic Productions, an appearance agency that counted the actor as one of its clients. His death was attributed to “old age”, with no other details provided. This article was amended on 26 October, 2026 to correct details on Koenig’s cameo on Star Trek: Picard.

headlines.title: Southern California prepares for flooding amid forecast of ‘record-breaking tides’
headlines.description: Residents of coastal towns told to avoid beaches during high tides and keep further away from the ocean than usual Southern California coastal communities are preparing for days of flooding amid potentially “record-breaking tides” this week. The National Weather Service warned that significant coastal flooding was expected in San Diego and Orange counties through Thursday that could close roads and inundate homes, businesses and critical infrastructure. To the north, a wide swath of the coast from San Luis Obispo county to Los Angeles county could see “minor to moderate” coastal flooding with tides as high as 8ft.

headlinePool.title: NHS consultants to go on two-day strike in England in November
headlinePool.description: Industrial action by senior doctors to begin on 25 November with only emergency cover provided, BMA says England’s most senior hospital doctors will strike next month in a dispute over their pay and hours, prompting NHS bosses to warn that patients will suffer “pain, discomfort and inconvenience”. Consultant doctors, who earn an average of £152,000 a year inclusive of overtime and merit awards, will stage a two-day walkout on 25 and 26 November, as hospitals gear up for the extra pressures winter brings.

headlinePool.title: No 10 clarifies Andy Burnham’s stance on freedom of movement
headlinePool.description: Clarification comes after PM fuelled speculation about EU-UK relationship in series of interviews at weekend Downing Street has been forced to clarify Andy Burnham’s stance on whether the UK would return to having freedom of movement with the EU after the prime minister said an “honest discussion” was needed on the issue. Burnham fuelled speculation about a return to freedom of movement in an interview at the weekend, prompting questions about how close the UK could become to Brussels.

headlinePool.title: Fifteen-year-old arrested in shooting near Florida university that injured 12
headlinePool.description: All but one of the victims sustained gunshot wounds as boy faces 11 charges of attempted second-degree murder A 15-year-old boy was remanded into secure detention in Florida on Monday charged with 11 counts of attempted murder following a mass shooting at a college homecoming party on Saturday. Six adults and six minors were injured, all but one with gunshot wounds, in the gunfire near the Florida Agricultural + Mechanical University (Famu) campus in Tallahassee.

headlinePool.title: Sydney's new $5bn airport has one big problem: Getting there is tough
headlinePool.description: The airport won’t have direct public transportation for a year. How do locals feel about getting there?

headlinePool.title: How the streets and social media drove Lula to a historic comeback in Brazil
headlinePool.description: A viral WhatsApp channel and student-led protests played a key role in the veteran Brazilian leftist’s election victory After the first round of the Brazilian presidential election three weeks ago, the leftist incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva reportedly told allies he could not understand how he finished second after a government he considered the best of his three terms. A mood of dismay swept Brazil’s left, and because 9 million voters for the other candidates, all of them on the right, were expected to mostly transfer to senator Flávio Bolsonaro, analysts widely saw the far-right senator’s victory as certain.

headlinePool.title: Jury selected for trial of four accused of sexually assaulting man’s drugged ex-wife
headlinePool.description: Mr Justice Saini tells the eight men and six women at Winchester crown court the case is likely to be upsetting Jurors being selected for the trial of four men accused of sexually assaulting the ex-wife of a former Conservative councillor, who has admitted repeatedly drugging and raping her, have been warned the case is likely to be upsetting. Philip Young, 50, has pleaded guilty to multiple charges of abuse against his former wife, Joanne Young, who has waived her right to anonymity.

headlinePool.title: Father pays tribute to son, six, killed by truck on Kansas soccer field
headlinePool.description: At funeral service Chris Adrian remembers son Cole as ‘capturing the heart’ of everyone, after tragedy killing two The father of Cole Adrian, a six-year-old boy killed when a woman drove through a soccer game at a park in Wichita, Kansas , on 17 October, paid an emotional tribute to his son at his funeral service on Monday. Chris Adrian, of McPherson, Kansas, spoke through tears while he remembered Cole as an energetic, fun-loving child who loved life and “captured the heart” of everyone he met.

headlinePool.title: How Lula beat far-right Bolsonaro in Brazil – The Latest
headlinePool.description: Brazil’s Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a historic fourth term as president, defeating the far-right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro in a dramatic comeback. Lula is the first candidate to win a runoff election after losing in the first round, taking victory with 51.79% of the vote to his rival’s 48.21%. His win bucks a regional trend, after the son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro had spearheaded a radical populist movement. But with Flávio Bolsonaro refusing to concede defeat, what’s next for Brazil? Michael Safi speaks to Latin America correspondent Tom Phillips – watch on YouTube

headlinePool.title: Shabana Mahmood launches review into murder of student Henry Nowak
headlinePool.description: Move comes after claims that killer had history of using threatening behaviour and an obsession with weapons Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, has launched a review to examine whether opportunities were missed to prevent the murder of the student Henry Nowak. It follows claims that there were several warning signs that the perpetrator, Vickrum Digwa, had a history of threatening behaviour and an obsession with weapons.
